subject: Re: Catalyst partnership — orchestration adapter & telemetry broker proposal
messages:
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia@catalyst.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Luis Ortega <luis@catalyst.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Catalyst x Redwood — initial integration proposal

Hi Rishi,

Really enjoyed the product walkthrough last week. Our engineering and GTM teams think there is a clear path to ship a joint product where Catalyst's prompt orchestration sits alongside Redwood's inference runtime.

High-level ask: we'd like to prototype an "adapter orchestration" (we call it Collector Broker) that:
- plugs into LangChain/LlamaIndex client flows (both Python + Node) to capture prompt/response traces,
- forwards a compact telemetry envelope to Redwood's telemetry ingestion API, and
- exposes a fallback routing shim so Catalyst-hosted flows can degrade to Redwood-hosted models in case of capacity spikes.

We sketched a proposal and attached a short spec + sequence diagram. Can you connect us to the right Redwood tech leads and let us know constraints around kernel selection, token attribution headers, and any SLOs we should expect?

Thanks,
Alicia

[attachment: catalyst-connector-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@catalyst.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Catalyst x Redwood — initial integration proposal

Alicia — thanks for the clear note and the spec. This direction aligns with our ISV playbook.

Quick alignment:
- We're happy to pilot a Collector Broker approach. Our goals for the pilot:
  * Validate low-overhead tracing for LangChain/LlamaIndex client calls (Python + Node),
  * Demonstrate token-level cost attribution and per-request routing fallbacks, and
  * Validate a secure envelope for telemetry (signed JWT + request id).

I'll loop in Priyom (runtime integrations) and Vanessa (partner success) to scope a 4-week POC. Priyom — can you review their sequence diagram and flag anything that will conflict with our batching or KV cache behavior? Also, what's the recommended header for passing through attribution (we typically accept X-RDW-Client-Id + X-RDW-Request-Id)?

Next steps:
1) Priyom to provide a tech checklist + compatibility matrix.
2) Joint repo created (Catalyst will open; Redwood will add a CI workflow).
3) Security questionnaire & quick SOC snapshot exchanged (Catalyst please share).

Happy to take a short call tomorrow 10am PT if that works.

—Rishi

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@catalyst.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Catalyst x Redwood — initial integration proposal

Alicia, Rishi — quick technical follow-up after reviewing the PDF and the prototype repo link. High-level comments and blockers:

1) LangChain/LlamaIndex hooking: we prefer a lightweight middleware approach rather than patching internal LLMPredictor classes. A single adapter that wraps call_async/call_sync and emits a compact trace (start_ts, model_variant, seq_len, prompt_hash) will be lowest-risk.

2) Token attribution: agree on using X-RDW-Client-Id + X-RDW-Request-Id. For attribution accuracy, Catalyst should include prompt chunk boundaries in the envelope so our KV cache heuristics can detect reuse.

3) Telemetry envelope size: keep under ~2KB per request for high-throughput pipelines. We'll batch envelopes server-side; ensure events include a deterministic request id for de-dup.

4) Runtime constraints: when requests route through Redwood's Dedicated fleet, we need to pass preferred kernel hints (e.g., quantized-int8 vs fp16) only as soft preferences — runtime will reselect based on seq_len distribution. Document these hints in the adapter config.

5) Security: we'll need a short SOC snapshot and an endpoint allowlist for the pilot. Also propose using mutual TLS for Collector Broker to Redwood ingestion endpoints.

I've attached a quick checklist and a proposed compatibility matrix. Would appreciate Catalyst's inputs on: supported client versions (LangChain >= 0.1.9, LlamaIndex >= 0.6.2), expected qps, and whether you want sampling for traces or full capture.

[attachment: collector-broker-sequence.png (PNG)]

From: Alicia Moreno <alicia@catalyst.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Luis Ortega <luis@catalyst.ai>, partners@catalyst.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Catalyst x Redwood — initial integration proposal

Thanks Priyom — great list. Answers inline: 

1) We'll build an adapter wrapper as you suggest. Catalyst will expose both a Python package and a Node package with identical telemetry envelope.

2) We'll emit prompt chunk metadata and preserve original request ids. We can include coarse token boundary markers to keep envelope size small.

3) For the pilot we expect ~30 qps (burst to 120) and prefer sampling at 10% across high-volume routes. We will also support full capture mode for a small subset of accounts.

4) Client versions: we can ship with LangChain 0.1.11 and LlamaIndex 0.6.3 compatibility layers.

5) Security packet: attached SOC snapshot and a short list of IPs for allowlisting. We can provision a mTLS cert for the Collector Broker.

We'll open the joint GitHub repo by EOD and include a readme with an adapter stub and example CI workflow.

Best,
Alicia

[attachment: security-snapshot-catalyst-2027.pdf (PDF)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Catalyst pilot — internal summary and next steps

Folks — brief summary after Catalyst's responses:

- Alignment: Catalyst will build a Collector Broker adapter for LangChain & LlamaIndex (Py/Node). They will include prompt chunk metadata and support sampling.
- Pilot scope (4 weeks): 1) integration test with Redwood's telemetry ingestion, 2) routing fallback demo (Catalyst -> Redwood model variant), 3) cost attribution report for sample workload.
- Blocks: Priyom flagged runtime hint semantics and envelope sizing; Catalyst agreed to keep per-envelope <2KB and use request ids for dedup. Security docs received.

Action items:
- Priyom: draft the adapter checklist and a minimal compatibility test matrix (due Tue next week).
- Vanessa: own partner success plan and customer-facing joint collateral (intro guide + reference architecture).
- Rishi: set up shared GitHub repo, CI template, and DocuSign for a simple pilot MOU (I will attach draft).

I'll schedule a kickoff for Monday 10am PT and invite Catalyst + our runtime and partnerships leads.

—Rishi

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
